newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Normans sees recovery in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Normans sees recovery in 2nd half.

text.p: Normans Wines Ltd said on Thursday it was an unlikely to see an immediate return to considerably stronger results in the first half of 1996/97 ending June 30.

"The board expects it will be the second half before the company's efforts really gather momentum and before this is evident in much more positive financial results," chairman Brian Burns told the annual meeting.
But when asked after the meeting if Normans expected to post a profit in 1996/97, chief executive officer Rob Byrne said: "Yes, we are."
Normans reported a net loss of A$867,000 in 1995/96, a result Burns told shareholders was quite unacceptable.
"I reassure you that the board is committed to an early return to sustained profitability through the growth and development of the company's branded products," he said.
Shareholders approved the issue on October 8 of 1.4 million shares or 8.7 percent of its issued capital to two investors, Ninety Second Macorp Nominees Pty Ltd and George Tauber Management Pty Ltd.

The meeting also approved further placements of up to 4.5 million ordinary shares in one or more tranches within the next three months, at an issue price of at least 80 percent of the ruling market price.
Burns said an injection of equity was desirable to reduce debt and gearing level.
"If we want to remain a major part of the Australian wine industry there is no doubt that we must grow through expansion, acquisition or merger," he said.
"The current capital raising efforts will give us the solid base we need to pursue this growth path," he said.
CEO Byrne later said Normans was more likely to achieve a friendly arranged merger with a large private wine company than an acquisition although it was not holding any talks at the moment.
Normans shares closed two cents lower at 78 cents on Thursday.
